svg.text: Conventional splits: one insertion, a chain of splits
A node splits when it overflows. The new sibling needs a slot in the parent; if the parent is full it splits too, and the chain continues up to the root.
Capacities here: 4 children per internal node, 6 entries per leaf. Keys are single letters.
insert j: its leaf L2 is full, and so is the parent R
full: j must go between i and k … no slot
full: no slot for a new child
the same insertion splits two existing nodes and creates a new root
1. L2 splits; j lands in L2′
2. R has no slot for L2′ → R splits
3. R′ has no parent → new root T
Why this is a problem for a resolver
The work of one write depends on how many of its ancestors happen to be full: usually none, sometimes every level. A batch that hits
such a path pays a latency spike, and the split cost is distributed unevenly across insertions. Proactive reservation removes the chain
by reserving parent capacity before it is needed, so that any write splits at most one existing node.
